best_for: People who meet on Jitsi often, on the public meet.jit.si or a company server, and want a desktop window that stays on top and allows remote control during screen sharing.

points.title: A desktop shell for Jitsi Meet
points.text: The app wraps the Jitsi Meet web client and works with any Jitsi server, not just meet.jit.si. Links like `jitsi-meet://server/room` open a room straight in the app.

points.title: Extras the browser lacks
points.text: It adds an always-on-top window and remote control during screen sharing, so a colleague can drive your desktop to help out.

points.title: Starting a meeting needs a login
points.text: On meet.jit.si, the first person in a room must sign in with Google, GitHub or Facebook, or wait for a moderator. Guests can join without an account.

points.title: Encryption has limits
points.text: Calls are encrypted in transit but decrypted in the Jitsi Videobridge's memory. End-to-end encryption is optional and covers audio, video and screen sharing only, not chat or polls.

points.title: Self-host to stay in control
points.text: Jitsi is free and Apache-licensed. Running your own server removes the need to trust meet.jit.si, and this app connects to it the same way.

points.title: Windows shows a warning
points.text: The README says Windows builds are unsigned, so expect a warning on first install. The installer is per-user, and the Windows listing keeps 63 versions; macOS (12 or later) and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is official
points.text: The Flathub build is published by the Jitsi Team and marked verified by Flathub, for x64 and Arm64. AppImage and .deb files are on GitHub too.
